Completion S-curve

Baseline vs. latest, cumulative —
Planned % complete Actual % complete Forecast % complete Earned (weighted) Contract finish Forecast finish Planned (period) Actual (period) Forecast (period, latest)
How this is built: each activity's loaded cost/weight × its planned schedule gives the Planned % curve, spread evenly across its baseline reference dates (its own actual date if already statused when the baseline was captured, else its target date). Actual spreads each activity's weight × current % complete between its actual start and finish (or the data date, if still open). The dashed Forecast continues from Actual by spreading the remaining weight across the current forecast finish — so it reaches 100% at whatever date the schedule now projects completion, which is what "planned vs. forecast completion" compares. The two dotted vertical lines mark Contract finish (blue, from the raw baseline file) and Forecast finish (orange), each labeled with its own date — the same two dates as the Key Dates card below, both read from whichever month is currently in view. Because a single schedule snapshot has no history, this approximates the curve's shape before today; its value at the data date is exact. The shaded band shows the gap between plan and where the project is actually tracking. The small bars along the bottom are that same Planned/Actual/Forecast data, differenced period-to-period instead of cumulative — how much moved in that one week or month, on the same % of total scale as the curves above. Forecast bars always read the latest upload, regardless of the month toggle above. Lines are drawn as a smoothed curve through the plotted points (a visual smoothing only — the underlying bucket values are unchanged), and data labels are shown at a decimated subset of points, matching the x-axis label spacing, to keep the chart readable.

How the weighting works

Each Level 2 WBS branch's share of the total — always adds up to 100%

Every activity carries a weight straight from P6 itself — its resource assignments and activity expenses, not anything typed in here. Add up the weight of every activity in a branch, divide by the project's total weight, and that's the branch's share below.

A branch's share is exactly how much it moves Overall Progress when it goes from 0% to 100% complete — the biggest branch swings the headline number the most, the smallest the least, no matter which one is actually behind. Same weight, same math, on every number this dashboard shows.
